_comment: FUND/ORG REGISTRY (the finance lookup) — resolves a fund_org to its Principal Invoicee(s).
'PI' here = Principal Invoicee, not necessarily a Principal Investigator: a department head,
a research PI, or a core director — whoever holds the fund and gets the bill. A fund can have
more than one. That is the ONLY thing OpenChargeback needs from finance to route an invoice.
No fallback chain and no fund-status routing live here. Fallback is ONE hop, handled entirely
in the license API: any unmapped user resolves to master_fund_org (see directory.example.json).
And whether a live fund can actually take a charge is finance's call at journal time, not ours —
an overdrawn or closed fund is theirs to re-home downstream.
One fund = one PDF, sent to that fund's invoicee(s), itemized by the users on it — so a PI can
forward a sponsored fund's statement straight to its funder with an annual report.
Codes follow a Banner-style fund-orgn convention (1xxxxx unrestricted, 2xxxxx sponsored; the
-NNNNN suffix is the owning org: 11045 = Computer Science, 11720 = Chemistry, 10000 = central).
Worked EXAMPLE populated from the Northwinds directory.

fund_orgs.name: Computer Science — Departmental Operating
fund_orgs._note: Dept-covered case. Two invoicees: the head owns it, the finance admin is copied. One PDF, sent to both, itemized by the faculty/staff/lecturers who charged to it. The individual is never billed; the head is.

fund_orgs.name: NSF #2431109 — Transom (Foundation Models for Scientific Reasoning)
fund_orgs._note: Grad-student case. The lab's seats roll up here; Transom gets ONE PDF, itemized by student, forwardable to NSF.

fund_orgs.name: NIH R01 #GM152050 — Selwick (Computational Reaction Design)
fund_orgs._note: Second department — the model isn't CS-specific.

fund_orgs.name: Office of Research — Master / Catch-all Fund
fund_orgs._note: The master_fund_org the license API emits for any username it doesn't recognize. Whatever lands here is Natterjack's to journal back to where it belongs. This is what guarantees a charge is never orphaned — one hop, not a chain.

fund_orgs.name: Provost's Office — AI Access Initiative (Subsidy)
fund_orgs._note: The subsidy owner's fund. When a subsidy covers part of a fund's usage, that covered slice is charged HERE — see subsidies.json for the cap rule. The subsidy rollup is PER FUND/ORG, not per user and not per usage: one line per subsidized fund showing how much of its cap the subsidy absorbed (e.g. 'covered $500 of Transom's grant'). Who used it is on that PI's own invoice, one level down.
